lifecycle.title: Bootstrap
gates: Every required integration is PRESENT, CLONED, PINNED or SNAPSHOT — or explicitly BLOCKED with a reason.
Skills are installed for the agent in use, and not duplicated across scopes.
The lock file exists and matches what is on disk.

lifecycle.title: Plan
gates: Acceptance criteria are testable and cover failure and unauthorized paths.
Every MUST CHANGE item has an owner file/module.
Rollback is written down.

lifecycle.title: Inspect
gates: You can describe the architecture without guessing.
Baseline build/test state recorded.
Sensitive operations and their current authorization are listed.

lifecycle.title: Threat model
gates: Every sensitive operation has a named server-side control.
Every abuse case has either a control or an explicit accepted risk with an owner.
The threat model is written to .biswodip/evidence/THREAT-MODEL.md, not held in your head.

lifecycle.title: Implement
gates: Every acceptance criterion has an implementation.
No security decision depends on client code.
Nothing in DO NOT CHANGE was modified.

lifecycle.title: Verify
gates: Every acceptance criterion has a passing test or an explicit UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED status.
No pre-existing failure was silently adopted as "expected".
Exit codes recorded, not paraphrased.

lifecycle.title: Design and accessibility
gates: Every interaction has real loading, empty, error and success states.
Keyboard-only walkthrough completed.
Reduced-motion verified.

lifecycle.title: Performance and context efficiency
gates: Before/after numbers recorded for every optimisation.
No security control, test or business rule removed for speed.
Expensive paths are bounded.

lifecycle.title: Security review
gates: Every applicable area reviewed with a status, not skipped silently.
Findings recorded with file and line.
Automated gate evidence saved under .biswodip/evidence/.

lifecycle.title: Authorized penetration testing
gates: Scope, authorization, mode, budget and run status recorded.
Every finding reproduced manually or dismissed with a reason.
Evidence written to .biswodip/evidence/.

lifecycle.title: Fix
gates: Every confirmed finding is FIXED or formally documented.
Every fix has a regression test.
No security control elsewhere was weakened to make the fix work.

lifecycle.title: Adversarial break test
gates: All applicable attacks attempted, with results recorded.
Every success is a finding in 10-fix.md.
Nothing was tested against a system you are not authorized to test.

lifecycle.title: Evidence matrix and score
gates: Matrix complete; no blank statuses.
Score computed from the matrix, with the caps applied.
Blocker list explicitly answered yes/no.

lifecycle.title: Release gate and report
gates: Every blocker in §33 answered from evidence.
Score, statuses and remaining risks stated.
Evidence locations listed so another engineer can re-check them.

commands.name: /dip
commands.description: Biswodip Goj Unified Engineering — auto-plans the goal, picks the few skills and stack it needs, runs subagents, verifies with evidence

commands.name: /dip-setapi
commands.description: Save the LLM gateway (base URL, API key, model) once; every /dip agent and tool picks it up automatically

commands.name: /dip:bootstrap
commands.description: Detect and install the five engineering integrations into this project

commands.name: /dip:design
commands.description: Design, accessibility and copy review — complete states, responsive, no AI slop

commands.name: /dip:handoff
commands.description: Write or refresh handoff.md so the next session resumes without losing context

commands.name: /dip:pentest
commands.description: Authorized penetration test (Strix + manual adversarial pass), then fix root causes

commands.name: /dip:plan
commands.description: Plan only — which few skills, stack entries and subagents this goal needs; changes nothing

commands.name: /dip:release
commands.description: Evidence matrix, weighted score with caps, blockers, and the final release report

commands.name: /dip:security
commands.description: Server-authoritative security review with an evidence-backed status per control

agents.name: @dip-backend
agents.description: Backend and data builder for /dip. Builds APIs, data models and migrations, cache, search, analytics and monitoring with the stack the plan chose (Prisma, Redis, Meilisearch, ClickHouse, TiDB, Netdata, Appwrite).

agents.name: @dip-browser
agents.description: Browser automation and crawling agent for /dip. Drives the browser with jev-ultrafast (instead of Playwright), falls back to Browser Use, and crawls with Crawlee (Node) or Scrapling (Python).

agents.name: @dip-frontend
agents.description: Web front-end builder for /dip. Builds UI, CSS, icons and animation with the stack the plan chose (Motion, Anime.js, Animate.css, Bootstrap, Font Awesome, css.gg, Impeccable, Front-End Checklist) and the design-review skill.

agents.name: @dip-infra
agents.description: Infrastructure and automation agent for /dip. Deployment, Kubernetes, scaling decisions, workflow automation with n8n, and multi-agent orchestration with Ruflo or Paperclip.

agents.name: @dip-mobile
agents.description: Mobile builder for /dip. Builds Android and iOS apps with React Native through Expo, with Appwrite (or the existing backend) for auth and data.

agents.name: @dip-planner
agents.description: Planning agent for /dip. Reads the repository and .biswodip/PLAN.md, confirms or cuts the proposed stack, writes acceptance criteria, and splits the work into tasks with one owner per file area. Use first in every /dip run, or when asked to plan a feature.

agents.name: @dip-quality
agents.description: Quality agent for /dip. Runs and adds tests, reviews the diff, draws the architecture, and enforces TDD and verification discipline (Keploy, Open Code Review, Archify, Superpowers, Matt Pocock skills).

agents.name: @dip
agents.description: Biswodip Goj Unified Engineering agent. Use for building, hardening, reviewing, auditing, pentesting or release-gating a repository, and whenever work must be backed by evidence rather than claims. Invoke with @dip.
